title: Fix strict replay comparison of large JSON integers
body:
The incorporated PR2040 strict comparator rejects valid 4,301-digit JSON integers under Python's default conversion limit, while accepting the same payload with that limit disabled. This adds an opt-in, source-pinned successor that parses integer tokens exactly without changing the process-global limit, and retains bounded typed diagnostics for unequal large integers.

Only `research/strict-payload-large-integers/` is added. The frozen comparator, immutable inputs and selected frontier stay intact. This is a portability repair; the large-number fixtures are synthetic and no supplier certificate failure, cold replay, performance gain or new kappa is claimed.

The successor compiles the bytes it authenticates and changes only the parser/diagnostic hooks. Complete integer values still decide equality; diagnostic hashes never decide acceptance. Duplicate keys, Boolean/integer/decimal distinctions, exact decimal values, unknown fields, array order, roots and declared timings retain the predecessor's rules. Ordinary integer parsing may cost more; resource hardening is outside scope.

Validation on macOS arm64:

- `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/strict-payload-large-integers` passed: original and successor reproduce the complete committed 105-file / 39-adverse / 22-deleted-timing receipt; 17 normal test groups and eight optimized groups pass.
- The new eight controls pass on CPython 3.11.15, 3.12.14, 3.13.12 and optimized 3.14.7. Real CLI processes cover limits 0/640/4300 and normal/optimized modes, exact integers up to 10,000 digits, unchanged process limits and low decimal precision, and one-digit/type/malformed/source-drift controls.
- Three broken successors (default parser, integer-as-decimal, unrepaired diagnostics) fail the controls. An optimized Git-free read-only 3.14.7 export passes the complete audit and 17 tests with all 20 exported files unchanged.
- Selected baseline source binding, package metadata/pins and diff checks pass. No Linux/Windows execution, hosted-CI success, independent human review or inherited theorem discharge is claimed.

Task `portable-replay`, priority 5; chooser nonce `28c18deb21d7b93b8314fb2d7044018f`. Started from canonical main `df801f6da7b9aa8e01bd35decde7b1b1d45eec08`; the pre-submission fetch remained there. Task, source hashes, exact scope and remaining caller-adoption question are in the package. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2800.

Final overlap refreshed 728 open PRs at 22:20 UTC on October 15, 2026. Discussion refresh was throttled and retained the complete 1,440-record snapshot from 22:15 UTC. No matching repair was identified; PR2693's paired traversal and PR2344's Windows roots are separate. These searches do not prove novelty.

Credit commdata2338 / PR2040 at `d31c1418c0c23994d1444dbd9d356b9a8238fd5e` for the strict comparator and retained audit; Josie Elliston / PR1824 for the portability predecessor; Maxime Fleury, Antoine Olivier and the credited supplier/archive lineage. Prepared for Arham Tahir with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in scoping, implementation, testing and writing. Apache-2.0; predecessor attribution and bytes preserved.

Publication checkpoint: canonical main advanced to `db3edc00f732806f663bfb9d4000567f18b17386`. Guidance, catalogue, selected record and all pinned comparator/archive inputs remain unchanged; the new main commit records supplier replay diagnosis and shared review dependencies. This additive package remains compatible without repinning frozen sources.

Coordination limitation: GitHub's GraphQL rate limit prevented updating Discussion2800 to DONE. The completed result and source head are recorded here; the original advisory claim expires at 00:20 UTC on October 16.
